Mrs. Fisher: I hope you didn’t get scared after catching your first flounder. They are quite bizarre, aren’t they.
You: Come on, there’s no way I would get scared of a fish. Who do you think I am?
Mrs. Fisher: A rookie.
You: …
Mrs. Fisher: When born, flounders look like normal fish, but as they mature one of their eyes migrates to the other side of the head. Thanks to that, flounders can see well while spending most of their lives on their side.
You: Why do they do that?
Mrs. Fisher: It’s evolution. They evolved that way a long time ago so that they can better camouflage on the ocean floor.
Mrs. Fisher: You can catch other flatheads around here too. Halibut is one of the biggest fish you can catch on these shores and just like flounder, it’s a flathead.
